QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_32

question.text: Following 25-April-2024, a Cat III AIF may launch a new Liquidation Scheme (close-ended scheme solely to liquidate unliquidated investments of an existing scheme): TRUE or FALSE?

answer.text: True — Liquidation Schemes are the preferred route post-2024
False — SEBI has notified no new Liquidation Schemes can be launched after 25-April-2024
True — but only if 90% of investors consent
False — Liquidation Schemes were never permitted in India

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 13.6.1: though the Liquidation Scheme modalities existed, SEBI has notified that NO AIFs shall launch any NEW Liquidation Schemes post 25-April-2024 (vide SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations 2024). The Dissolution Period now replaces the Liquidation Scheme as the route. The Trap: Option A is historically plausible but factually wrong post-April-2024. Option C invents a 90% threshold. Option D ignores the pre-2024 existence of Liquidation Schemes. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D test the 2024 Liquidation-Scheme sunset. Manager's Pro-Tip: For schemes with unliquidated investments at tenure end, architect the Dissolution Period pathway (with 75% consent + merchant-banker IM + DDC) rather than relying on Liquidation-Scheme memory from pre-2024 playbooks.
